title: Consumption fingerprinting for late-token events and quota corrections
creator: Maya Patel
description: Symptom: Console per-model breakdowns exhibit transient, high-amplitude spikes whenever delayed token events are backfilled from sharded ingest pipelines. Root causes are: (1) late events arrive without stable routing metadata and are attributed to the ingest shard that processed them rather than the original request context, and (2) current backfill job lumps all late tokens into the backfill ingestion timestamp which creates sharp spikes in daily charts and triggers quota/alerting thresholds incorrectly. This ticket proposes a new consumption fingerprinting layer and a smoothing attribution strategy so that late events are reconciled into historical windows without changing global billed totals.
impact: Customer-facing console charts show misleading per-model and per-tenant usage; several customers reported quota breaches driven by backfill spikes rather than real traffic. This affects billing accuracy, quota enforcement, and alerts for P1 customers. Expected revenue/billing totals remain unchanged, but per-model unit economics and SLA enforcement are currently unreliable.
proposed_fix: Introduce a deterministic fingerprint for each request bundle computed at ingest time using attributes available in the request path: (client_id, request_hash, model_alias, session_id if present, ingest_shard_id). Persist the fingerprint alongside canonical token tallies and event_uuid. Backfill pipeline will use fingerprints to: (a) attribute late token events to the original time bucket using a best-effort match; (b) when exact match missing, apply probabilistic assignment across candidate buckets weighted by observed session distributions; (c) emit idempotent correction events that carry both original_event_timestamp and correction_window. Update the billing subscriber to accept correction events that modify per-model/per-tenant breakdowns but do not change the total token sum for an invoice period. Add an exponential smoothing allocator that spreads backfilled tokens over the original 1h window by default (configurable per-customer).
acceptance_criteria: Backfill job run on a 7-day sample produces no >1% change in total billed tokens for the period
Per-model/per-tenant daily charts show no spikes >3x baseline after corrections in 95% of sample customers
Correction events are idempotent and safe to re-run from checkpoint without double-counting
Quota enforcement logic treats correction events as neutral for real-time enforcement but updates historical quota burn windows
Support tool exposes a reconciliation table with original_event_timestamp, attributed_bucket, and fingerprint for every corrected event
rollout_plan: 1) Implement fingerprint and correction event schema in ingestion service behind feature-flag. 2) Run internal dry-run backfill on non-prod clusters and validate reconciliation metrics. 3) Canary deploy to 5% of production customers for 7 days with console overlay showing adjusted vs raw charts. 4) If canary <1% errors, enable smoothing allocator globally for backfill-only runs. 5) After 2 weeks, flip billing consumer to accept historical breakdowns from correction events for analytics only (not invoice totals) and communicate to finance/support.
monitoring_and_telemetry: metric:backfill.corrections.ambiguous_fraction - fraction of corrections using probabilistic assignment
metric:console.per_model_spike_rate - rate of daily spikes >3x baseline after correction
log:reconciliation.audit - stores (fingerprint, original_ts, attributed_ts, model_alias, tenant_id, event_uuid)
blockers: Need updated event schema approved by data-platform and a migration plan for existing token tallies; dependent on sharded-ingest checkpointing work (coordination with ENG-61234).
